items.gist: The ahnika opens by presenting mantras as awakened through reflective awareness. It describes how independent consciousness confers agency on instruments and teachers.
It assigns seed syllables to foundational principles and elements. The sequence maps mantras onto the tattva hierarchy.
It details mantra limbs, faces, and ritual worship. Compact and expanded worship procedures are distinguished.
It presents Bhairava-related and maternal mantra forms. Their syllabic construction and ritual application are specified.
It discusses one-syllable mantras as supreme knowledge. Their subtle, hidden, and siddhi-bestowing uses are noted.
It introduces brahmavidya as immediately transformative. Recitation is said to free beings at death and remove fear.
It gives a series of Arya vakya utterances for bodily release. Each formula guides consciousness through successive centers.
It explains five-syllable and related mantra constructions. Their application follows the principle of pervasion.
It describes a Bhairava heart mantra for subduing powers. Its syllables and ritual deployment are carefully specified.
It addresses initiation for those lacking resources. Simplified rites and heart-centered remembrance are emphasized.
It enumerates initiatory vidyas and their syllabic forms. Each is linked to purification and spiritual attainment.
It presents three vidyas taught by Bhutiraja. Their forms and salvific functions are summarized.
It concludes that all mantra knowledge has been explained. The guru should apply prior principles without redundant repetition.
